advance.summary: For an explicitly supplied undirected graph with n vertices and m edges, nonnegative binary-rational exchange rates w_e, deterministic initial permutation (or multicolor/exclusion configuration), nonnegative binary-rational horizon T and accuracy 0<epsilon<=1, the manuscript proposes a classical sampler of one full endpoint within total-variation epsilon of the continuous-time interchange law. At each edge clock, endpoint labels exchange without bias or configuration-dependent rate. The claimed bit cost is polynomial in n,m,input bit lengths and 1/epsilon, independent of numerical T and original rates; it does not enumerate n! states or reconstruct joint law from one-particle marginals. This is a proof candidate, not implemented or benchmarked capability. The graph and rates are supplied explicitly, not succinctly encoded or physically acquired for free.
